question.text: Under the SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025 framework for co-investments within the AIF structure via a CIV scheme, which of the following is CORRECT?

answer.text: A CIV scheme may invest in up to 5 investee companies to diversify risk
CIV schemes may be offered to all investors of the AIF, including non-accredited ones
Each CIV scheme shall invest in only one investee company, and Angel Funds shall not launch any CIV schemes
Terms of co-investment in an investee company can be more favourable than the terms of investment of the AIF, reflecting the separate risk profile

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.9 and SEBI Circular dated September 9, 2025: (i) each CIV scheme shall invest in only one investee company, and (ii) Angel Funds shall not launch any CIV schemes. Co-investment is offered only to accredited investors, and CIV terms cannot be more favourable than the AIF's terms. The Trap: Multi-investee CIV contradicts the one-investee rule. Option C ignores the accredited-investor restriction. Option D directly contradicts the parity-of-terms rule. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests the older PMS-route; XIX-C tests the new CIV route introduced in 2025.
